item.title: Pennsylvania schools must teach cursive writing under bill signed by Governor Shapiro
item.description: Supporters of the bill say requiring cursive instruction will boost brain development and fine motor skills while helping students read historical documents and develop reliable signatures for legal and financial use. Critics argue schools should decide the most effective ways to teach written communication. item.title: Should students have voting power on Vermont’s school boards?
item.description: A Vermont bill, H.640, would require school boards that oversee high school grades to include student voting members, with one student per grade. Boards that operate middle schools would also add two nonvoting student members from grades 7 and 8. The post Should students have voting power on Vermont’s school boards? appeared first on District Administration.

item.title: Opinion: California schools that ban cellphones make students want them more
item.description: Blanket bans can punish students who use phones responsibly and may worsen overuse by making phones more tempting. They can also shift screentime to before or after class, when schools have less oversight. The post Opinion: California schools that ban cellphones make students want them more appeared first on District Administration.

item.title: Why one of North Carolina’s top school districts is eyeing closures
item.description: The Chapel Hill-Carrboro school board is considering closing up to two elementary schools as enrollment declines and budget pressures grow.
